name: a callable supplied as an argument is called by the other peer, and one returned in the result is called back
description: #196's example, whole, through generated code in both languages: the client hands the server a ProgressSink it implemented, the server calls report on it, the server answers a Job whose cancel and rename the client then calls. Neither peer sees a reference; both write and receive ordinary functions.

steps.note: ordinary RPC over a family that has a live tier: self-contained data, no binding made on either side
the request carries a callable and the result carries two
the server called the client's own function while start was still running
a callable returned in the result, called by the peer that received it, with a request and a result of its own
Job.cancel is an application operation; it is not release, and it is not cancelling the call that returned the job
